title: Platform architect — concise economics deck (WIP)
summary: A compact 6-slide lightning deck aimed at platform architects. Focus: tangible economic levers (batching, cache, quantization, routing) and a simple per-feature ROI worked example to accelerate pilot approvals. This is a WIP — need validation of pricing assumptions and a standard benchmark reference.
content:
Slide 1 — Title / TL;DR
- Title: Fast economic wins for platform architects
- TL;DR: 3 levers -> 2–5x token cost reduction while preserving 90% output parity for most QA/chat features. Use: pilot scoping + exec budget ask.

Slide 2 — Problem statement (engineer lens)
- Platform teams get requests for features (search, summarization, chat) but are blocked by unpredictable inference cost and latency.
- Typical ask: "Can we run this in our VPC?" + "What budget do we need?"
- Goal: give platform engineers a short, concrete checklist to convert feature ask -> capacity decision + ROI ask.

Slide 3 — The 3 economic levers (concise)
- Batching & concurrency: up to 3–4x throughput gains for batched text gen at moderate latency (10–200ms tail). Tradeoff: slightly higher p50 but much lower p95 cost.
- Prefix/KV caching: 30–70% token savings for repeated prompts or conversational state. Best for chat and multi-turn assistants.
- Quantization + model variant routing: 1.5–3x cost drop using INT8/4-bit runtimes and fallbacks to higher-precision for high-risk queries.
- Combined effect: compounding (example later).

Slide 4 — Worked ROI example (pilot: support summarization)
- Assumptions (draft, validate):
  - Expected weekly traffic: 25k requests, avg prompt+output tokens = 450 tokens
  - Hosted high-acc model cost: $0.0008 per token (baseline)
  - Target: reduce unit cost without increasing 95th latency beyond 300ms
- Baseline monthly cost: 25k * 450 * 4 weeks * $0.0008 = ~$36k/month
- Apply levers (conservative combined): batching -> 1.6x throughput (cost down 1.35x), caching -> 30% token reduction, quantized routing -> 2x cost reduction on 60% of traffic
- Rough conservative new monthly: ~$36k * 0.7 (cache) * 0.74 (batch) * 0.8 (routing mix) ≈ $14.8k (≈59% reduction)
- Outcome: Headline ask to infra budget: invest in 2 dedicated instances + small SRE runbook to implement caching and routing. Payback: under 2 months on committed capacity price delta vs. burst-hosted spikes.

Slide 5 — Talking points for architects / objections
- Objection: "Quality loss with quantization" -> Reply: can A/B 10% of requests to high-precision model and measure task-specific evals; fallback on confidence thresholds.
- Objection: "Operational complexity" -> Reply: Redwood provides rollout policies + canary routing; start with read-only cache & heuristic routing to reduce blast radius.
- Objection: "Vendor lock / compliance" -> Reply: show private deployment option with customer-managed keys; identical API surface.
- Quick ask to SE: "Can we get a 1-week test harness with sample traffic (CSV) and suggested SLOs?"

Slide 6 — Next steps & checklist (pilot playbook)
- 1) Collect sample traffic and 2–3 representative prompts (security review first).
- 2) Define quality eval (simple metric: ROUGE/F1 or human A/B on 200 examples).
- 3) Run micro-benchmark: baseline vs batched vs quantized on our canonical model (link to benchmark repo).
- 4) Calculate expected committed capacity and draft budget ask (use ROI calc sheet template).
- 5) Canaries: route 1% traffic to quantized model, monitor regression alerts for 72 hours.

Speaker notes / raw brainstorm (notes to self)
- Keep slides short; primary audience is platform architect who needs numbers for an internal ticket.
- Add a 1-line comfort statement about reliability & fallbacks.
- Need an internal benchmark slug: "avg-chat-512" with p50/p95 token distribution we can reference.
- Unresolved: pick conservative cost per token (is $0.0008 defensible?). Linked PR with cost estimates: github.com/redwood-inference/cost-models#pricing-assumptions
- Action: Priya to confirm hosted per-token numbers; Ibrahim to run quick quantized vs fp16 pass on sample model.

Appendix (optional) — Short glossary
- Prefix/KV cache: cache of model key-value memory for repeated prefixes (useful in chat).
- Quantized routing: route low-risk prompts to small-bit quantized variant; use confidence threshold for escalation.
- Throughput vs latency: batching increases throughput; must measure p95 impact.

Draft end — want input on: exact pricing assumptions, which benchmark to canonicalize, whether to include a short 1-slide ops runbook (yes/no).
